_anchors.canvas.w: 40. The widest obstacle is the kite balloon's envelope at 22 px plus fins; 9 px of margin a side holds the outline.
_anchors.canvas.h: 52. The kite balloon reaches 37 px above the line and the mooring tails reach 7 below it — the one place any obstacle paints below the horizon, and it is a depth cue, not a footprint.
_anchors.canvas.originY: 44 — the cruise line. Obstacles anchor by origin on the runner's ground row, so the origin IS the horizon: art above it is obstacle, art below it is rope trailing toward the far world.
_anchors.frames.walk: 1: the balloon and the kite balloon are moored stills, as the gravestones and the kerbs were. The flock animates and carries its own file, the cat-tuck rule.
_anchors.light.x: -0.5, the scene's lamp, shared with the machine.
_anchors.gait.roll: 0. Nothing in the furniture rolls; the channel belongs to the machine.
_anchors.body.scale: 1: furniture at the world's own scale.
_anchors.shadow.steps: 7, shared with the machine so one sun lights the sky.
_anchors.fill.x: 0.45, opposite the key, the scene's fill.
_anchors.playback.msPerFrame: 125, read only by the bench for a 1-frame still.
_anchors.outline.material: "ink", the same line as the machine: one hand draws the sky.
_anchors.outline.inner: true; welds mark the real seams — basket against envelope, cable against everything.
